title: US federal performance management: FAPA implementation audit

sourceCatalog.reuse: GAO states federal-authored work is public domain in the US; third-party images may require separate permission; only original factual summaries recorded

observations.measure: OMB August 2025 guidance fully addressed 10 of 15 FAPA strategic-review requirements
observations.population: 15 statutory requirements; GAO assessment of guidance
observations.note: GAO-26-108516; no inference of corruption, individual guilt, service failure or causal trust effect.

observations.note: GAO-26-108516; no inference of corruption, individual guilt, service failure or causal trust effect.

observations.measure: Selected agencies not conducting required strategic reviews in 2025
observations.population: Four purposively selected agencies; agencies reported different explanations
observations.note: GAO-26-108516; no inference of corruption, individual guilt, service failure or causal trust effect.

observations.measure: OMB had addressed 14 of 17 prior GAO recommendations related to CAP goals by June 2026
observations.population: 17 past CAP-goal recommendations; positive accountability counterexample
observations.note: GAO-26-108516; no inference of corruption, individual guilt, service failure or causal trust effect.

events.subject: Office of Management and Budget
events.finding: OMB established crosscutting goals in December 2025 within the first year of the administration.
events.disposition: GAO later found remaining implementation and reporting gaps.

events.subject: OMB, DHS, Treasury, State and GSA
events.finding: GAO found OMB guidance incomplete and none of four selected agencies fully addressed new strategic review requirements.
events.disposition: GAO recommended guidance and agency process improvements; four agencies agreed, OMB provided no comments. Implementation not established.

limitations: Four selected agencies were purposively chosen from 13 in earlier GAO work; no population prevalence inference.
The 10/15 guidance score concerns statutory coverage, not realized service outcomes.
Agreement with recommendations is not evidence of implementation.
No causal inference about public trust or personal wrongdoing.
